commit.message:
chore(release): bump version to v1.4.1

Hotfix release for the exhaustive-element inference bug (c956c0a): every
Transformer in a model with an untracked ash fraction was discarding the
non-carbon share of DM. Affects v1.3.5 and v1.4.0; biomass models should
upgrade and re-run rather than reinterpret their results.

Untracks T18_Alloying_Element_Accumulation and its golden reference. The
fix exposed a defect in T18's own config — Recycling retains Cu (1.0)
harder than the DM containing it (0.5) while F_05_01 keeps feeding copper
in, so Cu accumulates past its own parent and the solve does not converge.
The overwrite had been pinning DM to Cu and hiding it. Kept locally via
.gitignore rather than deleted, so it can return once its transfer
coefficients give Cu a sink. The golden parametrisation globs the working
tree, so a fresh clone simply does not produce that case.

The v1.4.1 stabilization scope planned 2026-07-29 moves to v1.4.2.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

-schema_version: '1.0'
-name: T18_Alloying_Element_Accumulation
-description: '📘 Tutorial T18 — Tramp-element accumulation via Input_Substitution
-
-
-  Fully exploits the two-flow Input_Substitution mechanism: recycled steel scrap is
-  more contaminated with copper (a tramp/alloying element that conventional refining
-  cannot remove) than virgin ore-derived steel. Because the consumed (recycled) and
-  residual (virgin) flows are separate, each carries its own composition — Manufacturing''s
-  blended copper content genuinely shifts over time as the recycled share grows, exactly
-  the down-cycling effect steel recyclers worry about in the real world.
-
-
-  What it shows
-
-  • Steel Manufacturing needs a flat 100 Mg/yr of steel (DM), defined on the Input
-  Flow Time Series page.
-
-  • Recycled scrap supply ramps from 30 up to 220 Mg/yr — crossing the 100 Mg/yr target
-  partway through the horizon.
-
-  • Virgin steel carries 0.05% Cu (clean ore); recycled scrap carries 0.6% Cu (accumulated
-  tramp copper from prior product life cycles).
-
-  • Once scrap supply exceeds the target, virgin extraction drops to zero and the
-  excess scrap is diverted to Low-Grade Scrap Export instead of displacing more virgin
-  steel than is needed.
-
-
-  Try it
-
-  • Open Input Flow Time Series to see both the scrap ramp and the flat demand target,
-  defined exactly the same way.
-
-  • Compare F_01_02 (virgin residual) and F_01_02_2 (consumed/recycled) — same downstream
-  process, different composition each.
-
-  • Change the scrap composition (flow_compositions on F_00_01) and re-watch how Manufacturing''s
-  blended Cu content responds.
-
-
-  Look for
-
-  • Manufacturing''s blended copper content rises from ~0.22% (mostly virgin, slightly
-  diluted by early recycled content) toward 0.6% as the recycled share grows — then
-  plateaus at exactly the scrap''s own 0.6% once scrap supply first reaches the 100
-  Mg/yr target, because virgin extraction has bottomed out at zero and cannot dilute
-  it any further.
-
-  • Low-Grade Scrap Export (F_01_03) stays at zero until scrap supply crosses the
-  100 Mg/yr target, then absorbs everything beyond it.
-
-  • Virgin residual (F_01_02) and consumed (F_01_02_2) always sum to exactly 100 Mg/yr
-  — the fixed demand target — regardless of the scrap ramp.'

+## [1.4.1] - 2026-08-27
+
+Hotfix release. **Anyone running a biomass model on v1.3.5 or v1.4.0 should
+upgrade and re-run**: those versions silently deleted the non-carbon share of
+dry matter at every `Transformer`, and the results are wrong rather than merely
+imprecise.
+
+### Fixed
+- Engine: **mass loss at every `Transformer` in models with an untracked
+  ash fraction**. `system_setup._infer_exhaustive_elements` marked a parent
+  element complete as soon as *one* flow declared its children summing to
+  1.0. Biomass models trip this structurally: atmospheric carbon uptake is
+  declared as TC/CC = 100% of DM on the boundary flow — that flow really is
+  pure carbon — while every other flow carries TC at ~45% of DM with
+  `Ash_content` untracked. DM was therefore read as exhaustive, and since
+  v1.3.5 the solver derives every exhaustive parent from its children, so
+  `DM := TC` on each transformation and the ash fraction was discarded
+  (−55% of DM in the affected studies, propagating into `material` and into
+  every downstream process). A node is now exhaustive only when the flows
+  declaring its children **agree** — some flow sums to 1.0 and none
+  contradicts it; inconsistent evidence is reported partial. Affects
+  v1.3.5 and v1.4.0 only.
+
+### Removed
+- Tutorial **T18_Alloying_Element_Accumulation** and its golden reference are
+  no longer shipped. The fix above exposed a defect in its own configuration:
+  Recycling retains Cu (1.0) harder than the DM containing it (0.5) and
+  `F_05_01` keeps feeding copper in, so Cu accumulates without bound and the
+  solve does not converge. The overwrite had been pinning DM to Cu and hiding
+  it. The tutorial returns once its transfer coefficients give Cu a sink.
+
+### Notes
+- The v1.4.1 stabilization scope planned on 2026-07-29 (parity closeout, Monte
+  Carlo coverage gaps, Dashboard↔Workflow parity) moves to **v1.4.2** — this
+  number was taken by the hotfix.
+
+---
